problem: The value $V(t)$ of a tech device varies according to the differential equation ${V}^{′}(t)=-rV(t),$ where $t$ is the time, measured in years, and $r>0.$ It is known that the value reduces by one-half after the first year. How long does it take for the value to reduce to one-fifth of its original value? Round your answer to one decimal place.
worked_solution:
The general solution to the given differential equation is

$$
V(t)={V}_{0}{e}^{-rt},
$$

where ${V}_{0}$ is the value when $t=0.$

Let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the value equals $\frac{1}{5}{V}_{0}.$ Then, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}V({t}_{1}) & =\frac{1}{5}{V}_{0}\,⇒\,{V}_{0}{e}^{-r{t}_{1}}=\frac{1}{5}{V}_{0}.\end{aligned}
$$

We solve this equation for ${t}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{0}{e}^{-r{t}_{1}} & =\frac{1}{5}{V}_{0} \\ \cancel{{V}_{0}}{e}^{-r{t}_{1}} & =\frac{1}{5}\cancel{{V}_{0}} \\ {e}^{-r{t}_{1}} & =\frac{1}{5} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-r{t}_{1}}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{5}) \\ -r{t}_{1} & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ {t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{r}\,\,(∗)\end{aligned}
$$

We now need to calculate $r.$ We're told that the value reduces by one-half after the first year. Therefore,

$$
V(1)=\frac{1}{2}{V}_{0}\,⇒\,{V}_{0}{e}^{-r}=\frac{1}{2}{V}_{0}.
$$

We solve this equation for $r,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{0}{e}^{-r} & =\frac{1}{2}{V}_{0} \\ \cancel{{V}_{0}}{e}^{-r} & =\frac{1}{2}\cancel{{V}_{0}} \\ {e}^{-r} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-r}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}) \\ -r & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ r & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this into $(∗)$ and evaluating, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{r} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & ≈2.3,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
